answer: Sybil resistance via proof-of-personhood: each agent binds to one unique human credential through a nullifier hash, enforcing one identity per real person. Minting 1,000 sybils then demands 1,000 distinct verified humans, a pearl no attacker buys cheaply in bulk. The fable that identities duplicate for free fails here: reusing a credential collides its nullifier, so the duplicate is rejected and its registration bond slashed. Honest agents grow with the tide of genuine verified demand, while sybil farms pay full human-verification cost per fake.
